Expenditure

ik-SPEN-dih-chur — contains 'spend'; an expenditure is simply money spent. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Expenditure is an amount of money that is spent, or the act of spending it.

The family's biggest monthly expenditure was rent, followed closely by groceries.

Worked Example

A nonprofit publishes its yearly financial report, listing exactly how much it paid for staff salaries, office rent, and printing costs. Donors can see precisely where every dollar went.

The itemized list of exactly what money went out the door is the organization's expenditure. Unlike 'budget,' which is a plan for future spending, expenditure describes money that has actually been paid out.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spending: Spending is the everyday word for paying money out, and it usually stays general and uncountable — too much spending, holiday spending. Expenditure is the formal, countable term that budgets and reports prefer: an organization lists its expenditures line by line and compares them against income.

outlay: An outlay is money put down up front for a particular purpose — the initial outlay for equipment or a food truck. Expenditure is the wider ledger word for any money paid out, one-time or ongoing: every outlay is an expenditure, but monthly rent is expenditure, not an outlay.

disbursement: A disbursement is a payment sent out of a fund to a recipient — an insurance payout after a storm, an author's advance from a publisher. Expenditure describes money from the spender's own books: the totals an organization reports having paid out. The money reaches you as a disbursement; the payer records an expenditure.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

income: money received, especially regularly

revenue: income generated from business activity

Where it sits · the scale and excess of spending — cost → expenditure → extravagance

cost vs. expenditure: Cost is narrower than expenditure — a cost is the price of one single thing, while expenditure can describe an entire organization's total spending across everything.

extravagance vs. expenditure: Extravagance goes further than expenditure: expenditure is simply money spent, but extravagance is spending far more lavishly than necessary.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-

prefix — ex-: out (Latin)

root — -pend-

root — -pend-: to weigh, to pay (Latin)

suffix — -iture

suffix — -iture: result of an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin pendere meant 'to weigh' — since coins were once weighed out to determine payment, ex- (out) plus pendere gives 'weighed out,' which became 'paid out.' Expenditure is money that has been paid out.

Use the root in a new word: suspend

Use the root in a new word: suspend: The referee decided to suspend the game until the storm passed.
